themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 14 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 918% increase (z-score: 14.73)—suggesting a coordinated campaign or sudden enforcement gap in Forest Hills/Rego Park.
evidence: 14 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
918% spike with z-score of 14.73 (statistically extreme deviation)
No prior news coverage or community board discussion of this issue
reporting_angles: Ground-truth: Visit hotspot locations to document what is being posted (flyers, tags, construction notices, political material) and interview residents about impact
Enforcement angle: Contact DSNY and 311 to determine if there's a known source or if this reflects a systemic enforcement lag

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 16 THIS WEEK against a baseline of 5.5 per week—a 191% spike (z-score: 3.5)—signaling a possible outbreak or unsanitary conditions emerging in the district.
evidence: 16 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Community board has standing request to expand street outreach and sanitation, suggesting long-term underlying issues
reporting_angles: Resident interviews: Find affected blocks and talk to people about sightings, timing, and what triggered the outbreak
DSNY response: Request data on recent rodent baiting schedules and whether Forest Hills/Rego Park is under-resourced compared to other districts

themes_detail.label: Traffic Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Traffic-related complaints surged to 12 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 3.0 per week—a 300% jump (z-score: 3.75)—coinciding with four active rezoning applications that may be driving construction or congestion.
evidence: 12 traffic complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks

Four active ULURP rezoning applications (Yellowstone Boulevard, 108-05 68th Road, 100-12 Queens Boulevard, 69-67 108th Street) plus 306 DOB permit filings in last 90 days suggest construction activity
reporting_angles: Construction impact: Map the four rezoning sites and interview residents on affected blocks about congestion, double-parking, and truck traffic
Developer coordination: Request data from DOB and DCP on whether permits are clustered and whether a traffic management plan exists across projects

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage and Overgrown Branches
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints hit 5 THIS WEEK (344% above the 1.1 weekly baseline, z-score: 4.96), while overgrown tree/branch complaints reached 7 three weeks ago (195% above baseline, z-score: 2.93)—suggesting neglect or storm damage in the district's green infrastructure.
evidence: 5 illegal tree damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (344% spike, z-score: 4.96)
7 overgrown tree/branch complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.4 weekly average (195% spike, z-score: 2.93)
Community board repeatedly requests park and amenity expansion, signaling under-resourced green space maintenance
reporting_angles: Visual audit: Walk major streets to document tree damage, dead limbs, and overgrowth; compare to adjacent districts
Parks Department accountability: Request maintenance schedules and staffing levels for Forest Hills/Rego Park vs. other CD districts

themes_detail.label: Panhandling Complaints Emerge
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints jumped to 6 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 0.6 per week—an 860% spike (z-score: 7.72)—reflecting possible homelessness or street outreach gaps that the community board has flagged repeatedly in budget requests.
evidence: 6 panhandling complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (860% spike, z-score: 7.72)
Community board has standing budget request to expand street outreach (Department of Homeless Services) and Fair Fares (transit assistance)
No prior news coverage of homelessness in Forest Hills/Rego Park
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: Identify which blocks/transit hubs are seeing panhandling and interview residents about their perception of public safety
Services gap: Contact DHS and local nonprofits to determine if outreach teams are stationed in or regularly visit Forest Hills/Rego Park
